> Everything so far has been preparation for this: a real dataset, a real
> question, and a real problem that no method can fix.

## About this section

You will work a genuine study end-to-end — from haplogroup calls to a
hypothesis test, and then to the discovery that the test cannot be interpreted.

This is not a contrived teaching example. It is a real cohort from Botswana,
and the flaw you will find is a real flaw in a real analysis.

## The session

| | Activity | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Case study: mtDNA haplogroups & HIV status](1-mtdna-case-study/index.qmd) | 90 min |
| 2 | Group discussion: what would you do next? | 30 min |
| 3 | Bring your own data clinic | 60 min |

## What you will do

Load 338 participants with HaploGrep 3 haplogroup calls and HIV status. Wrangle,
visualise, build a contingency table, run the test — the standard workflow from
[Section 2](../2-ai-application/index.qmd).

Then run one more line of code and discover that the study design is confounded
beyond repair.

::: {.callout-important}
## Why we teach a broken dataset
Every teaching dataset you have ever met was chosen because it behaves. That is
why analysts are unprepared for real data.

The skill worth having is not running a test. It is knowing whether the test
means anything. You cannot learn that on clean data.
:::

## Bring your own data

The last hour is unstructured. Bring a dataset and a question. The most useful
thing we can do is help you find the problem in *your* data before a reviewer
does.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Come with the awkward question
The dataset you are unsure about is more valuable here than the one you have
already published.
:::
